tasks.title: Telemetry analysis notebook
tasks.goal: Explain a measured request population without hiding assumptions.
steps: Extract the bundle; all files are flat inside the named practice folder.
Read README.md and run the baseline commands.
Define measurement boundaries and units.
Classify counters, gauges and distributions.
Calculate nearest-rank percentiles.
Write safe structured log fields.
Interpret golden signals and nested spans.
Record actual outputs and compare them with the rubric; do not claim unexecuted checks.
Optional: read mechanism-lab.md and run the real mechanism drill if its prerequisites are available.

commands.label: Check foundation percentile reasoning
commands.expected: Three tests pass for nearest rank, preserved inputs and invalid sample handling. SLO and HTTP experiments follow in the next stage.

commands.label: Optional mechanism drill (read its guide first)
commands.expected: Two measured JSON timelines, one success and one error, followed by PASS for timeline bounds and error evidence. Timings vary.

steps: Extract the bundle; all files are flat inside the named practice folder.
Read README.md and run the baseline commands.
Run healthy, slow and fail profiles.
Compare counts, errors and latency.
Define good and eligible events.
Calculate error budget and burn rate.

Benchmark equivalent lookup implementations.
Record actual outputs and compare them with the rubric; do not claim unexecuted checks.

commands.label: Run local reference checks
commands.command:
python telemetry.test.py
python integration.test.py
python benchmark.py
commands.expected: Seven analysis checks and real loopback HTTP integration pass; equivalent lookup implementations report repeated actual timings. Port 8891 must be free for integration.test.py.

commands.label: Terminal 1: start the local service
commands.expected: Service listens on loopback port 8891 until Ctrl+C. Keep this terminal open.

commands.label: Terminal 2: compare the three profiles
commands.command:
python load.py --profile healthy
python load.py --profile slow
python load.py --profile fail
commands.expected: Each command finishes after 20 requests. Fail reports four HTTP failures. Slow adds delay to every fifth response; actual timing varies. Stop terminal 1 with Ctrl+C afterward.

prerequisites.label: Finish this stage through 14. Benchmark a hypothesis rather than a favourite optimisation
